summary: Brief verification of the Solicitor Sanity Check 'Coming soon' gate. Backend: GET /api/sanity-checks/availability -> {available:false}; POST /api/sanity-checks/create-and-checkout (authenticated test@advocate.app) -> 503 'Solicitor Sanity Check is coming soon — no charge has been made.' Frontend: logged in as test@advocate.app, opened Ask Lex via dashboard tile, asked 'Can my landlord keep my deposit?'. Under Lex's answer the disabled button data-testid=sanity-soon-1 'Solicitor check · Coming soon' rendered (disabled=true); no sanity-{i} gold button and no '£49' text anywhere. Clicking it did nothing (URL unchanged, no create-and-checkout / Stripe request fired). 'Their argument' button still renders. 0 console errors, no crash.
action_items: (Before going live) In the live sanity-{i} onClick, `if (!aaConfirm(...)) return;` — aaConfirm returns a Promise, so `!promise` is always false and the confirm dialog is bypassed; use `if (!(await aaConfirm(...))) return;`. Not reachable today because the gate hides it.

(Before going live) SANITY_ELIGIBLE_FIRM_Q only matches billing_status/billing_tier set by Stripe webhooks. Comped/trial firms (e.g. founder.demo@aiadvocate.co.uk uses tier/trial_tier/trial_until, no billing_* fields) will never make the feature available. Decide if that's intended.
critical_code_review_comments: SanityGate module cache (__sanityAvail) is only set after the request resolves, so 2 GET /availability calls fire when several messages mount at once. Harmless; could cache the promise instead.
SanityGate caches availability for the whole page session, so once firms sign up, existing sessions keep showing 'Coming soon' until reload. Acceptable.
seed_data_creation: None. No Stripe sessions or firm accounts created (503 returned before any DB insert).
context_for_next_testing_agent: UI login: set localStorage aa_token + aa_terms/aa_welcomed/aa_uk_scope_ack/aa_lex_upl_ack=1, aa_cookie_consent=essential, sessionStorage aa_splash_seen=1, goto '/'. For free users, bottom-nav 'nav-lex' opens the subscribe modal (hasAccess false); use dashboard 'tile-ask_lex' to open chat (chat-input / send-btn). The Lex answer index was 1 (sanity-soon-1).
